dataset.readme:
# ICMarkingSynthetic 1.0

Synthetic IC marking images and labels. Start with docs/LOADING.md and DATASET_CARD.md.

The balanced collection has 6,000 images, 6 image classes, 4 defect classes and 40 openly licensed source packages. The 467 cosmetic examples and 18 auxiliary clean counterparts are separate and must not be counted in the balanced collection.

Images: CC BY-SA 4.0; annotations and provenance: CC BY 4.0. Preserve source attribution from SOURCES.csv.

Saved masks represent renderer support. They are not guaranteed to contain every changed pixel. In the recovered counterpart subset, 18 of 38 pairs contain all changes of at least two gray levels within a one-pixel dilation of the saved mask; all 38 changed-pixel counts match provenance. Masks were preserved, not repaired. Polygons describe external contours and may omit holes or smaller disconnected regions. The sha256 provenance field is a 16-character prefix of the decoded pixel hash, not a PNG-file hash; use CHECKSUMS.sha256 for file integrity.

code.name: icmarkingsynthetic-generator-v1.0.zip
code.readme:
# icmarkingsynthetic-generator 1.0

Implementation of the physics-informed guidelines by Md Sami Ul Hoque and
Nasser Kehtarnavaz, Embedded Machine Learning Laboratory, University of Texas at Dallas.
Numerical renderer functions are extracted from the implementation used for the
dataset. Only the frozen scratch and contamination parameter sets are included.
No real evaluation images, per-frame measurements or reference-frame names are included.

## Installation and use

Use Python 3.12 and run `python -m pip install -e .` from this directory.
The dependencies are pinned to the environment used for the packaging tests.
From this directory, with the dataset extracted alongside it:

```text
python scripts/regenerate_image.py --dataset ../ICMarkingSynthetic-v1.0 --id TVIC29_C000_scratch --output regenerated
python scripts/run_validator.py --dataset ../ICMarkingSynthetic-v1.0
python scripts/calibrate_profile.py --reference reference_measurements.json --synthetic synthetic_measurements.json --kind scratch --output comparison.json
```

The calibration inputs are lists of descriptor dictionaries measured from data
you are authorized to use. Reference measurements are intentionally not distributed.
Scratch comparison retains the original rank-order AUC computation, whose handling
of exact ties can affect its value. Contamination uses half-credit ties. Do not
interpret a calibration pass as independent real-world validation.

## Reproduction and scope

The `sources/` directory contains the 40 prepared, openly licensed masters and
their approved face, marking and surface-feature masks. Source attribution and
the preparation modifications are listed in SOURCES.csv. The code starts from
these prepared arrays. It does not claim to repeat all historical, manually
reviewed photographic cleanup from the original Wikimedia photographs.
`prepare_source.py` derives region masks for an already prepared image and a
provisional marking mask; inspect all outputs before using a new source.

`build_release.py` renders the selected main-image generation plan and emits
images, face crops, masks, box/polygon labels, COCO, classification files, split
lists, YAML files and provenance. Cosmetics and additional clean counterparts are
saved separately. It is a renderer, not an archive publisher: documentation,
source attribution, license texts and ZIP files are supplied in the dataset
archive rather than regenerated by this command.

Determinism within a tested runtime does not guarantee byte-identical reproduction
of the distributed images in a different runtime. A prior recovery audit found
pixel discrepancies when regenerating clean captures; original archived PNGs
were retained for the dataset. The regeneration command reports the actual pixel
hash and whether it matches the released hash. Add `--require-exact` to fail on a
mismatch. Never replace the distributed clean counterparts with approximate renders.

Saved masks represent renderer support, not an exhaustive map of every changed
pixel. Labels include only visible instances meeting the original gates. External
polygons can omit holes and secondary disconnected components. These limitations
are also explained in the dataset documentation.

## Modules and parameters

region: approved surface regions; capture: affine, photometric, optics and noise;
defects: abrasion, deposition and photographed-glyph changes; severity: levels;
labels: visibility, instances, boxes and polygons; descriptors and calibrate:
measurement comparison; seeding: independent hashed random streams; validate:
structural and digest checks. Profile JSON files document the frozen constants
embedded in the corresponding modules; editing JSON alone does not change rendering.

Software is MIT. Prepared source images and their image derivatives are CC BY-SA
4.0 with per-source attribution. Dataset annotations/provenance are CC BY 4.0.
The software license does not replace the image licenses.

documents.docs/SPLITS.md:
# Split protocols

The images/train, val and test folders implement the source-disjoint split; sources remain exclusive. splits/source_disjoint.json records it. Product-matched split files contain image IDs; corresponding .images.txt files contain relative paths for Ultralytics. All images with the same capture_group stay in one subset. Never randomly split related images. Auxiliary counterparts and cosmetics are not added to evaluation counts.

Run from the relevant full-image or face_crop directory so path: . resolves there. Both views use identical image IDs and membership.
documents.docs/LOADING.md:
# Loading

```python
from pathlib import Path
import json
from PIL import Image
root = Path('ICMarkingSynthetic-v1.0')
records = [json.loads(s) for s in (root/'provenance/records.jsonl').read_text().splitlines()]
r = records[0]
image = Image.open(root/r['image'])
mask = Image.open(root/r['mask'])
assert image.size == mask.size == (640, 320)
```

For box detection, change the current directory to the dataset root, then use `YOLO('yolov8n.pt').train(data='dataset.yaml')` with the Ultralytics package. Use dataset_product_matched.yaml for the other protocol. For face crops, change directory to face_crop first. For segmentation, create a separate working copy and replace labels/train, labels/val and labels/test with copies of labels/polygons/train, val and test. Do not change the distributed archive. The extra box-label aliases do not introduce extra images or instances.
documents.DATASET_CARD.md:
# ICMarkingSynthetic

Authors: Md Sami Ul Hoque and Nasser Kehtarnavaz, Embedded Machine Learning Laboratory, University of Texas at Dallas.

Purpose: research on synthetic marking defects, detection and automatic labeling. Defects are cause-derived image-formation approximations, not first-principles material simulations. This archive contains synthetic images from openly licensed source photographs, not real evaluation frames. Missing and smeared text lack real-image evaluation in the reported study. Results are not evidence of factory readiness.

Composition:
```json
{
  "by_class": {
    "good": 1000,
    "scratch": 1000,
    "contamination": 1000,
    "missing_text": 1000,
    "smeared_text": 1000,
    "combined": 1000
  },
  "source_disjoint": {
    "train": 3605,
    "val": 1204,
    "test": 1191
  },
  "product_matched": {
    "train": 4569,
    "val": 716,
    "test": 715
  }
}
```

Saved masks represent renderer support. They are not guaranteed to contain every changed pixel. In the recovered counterpart subset, 18 of 38 pairs contain all changes of at least two gray levels within a one-pixel dilation of the saved mask; all 38 changed-pixel counts match provenance. Masks were preserved, not repaired. Polygons describe external contours and may omit holes or smaller disconnected regions. The sha256 provenance field is a 16-character prefix of the decoded pixel hash, not a PNG-file hash; use CHECKSUMS.sha256 for file integrity.

See SOURCES.csv for source licenses and modifications; no source photograph is asserted to be public domain merely because it is openly accessible.
